passages.provision_quote: (b) The general assembly may amend the congressional districts 7 established under subsection (a) at a time other than the first 8 regular session of the general assembly convening immediately 9 following the United States decennial census.
passages.note: Engrossed bill text: the legislature itself amends congressional districts mid-decade, adds a new 2026 map (IC 3-3-7) and limits judicial relief in apportionment challenges, so the instrument speaks to who draws the lines, but Bray voted against it.
Official bill page naming the authors and Senate sponsors (Bray is neither) and recording that the bill was defeated on Senate third reading.
Senate roll call 8 lists Bray among the 31 Nays, the only page that shows his act; the 31-19 split means this is not a near-unanimous vote.

rows.reasoning: Bray is listed in the Nay column of Roll Call 8 on HB 1032 (2026), the mid-decade redistricting bill under which The general assembly may amend the congressional districts outside the post-census session and a new 2026 congressional map would take effect; it was defeated 19-31. The No vote tells against the party that controls the state legislature without outside interference, but it matches no clause of any remaining rung: he may object to a mid-decade redraw, to the bill's limits on judicial relief, or to this particular map while still accepting districts drawn by state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias. No source here gives his own words on who should draw the lines, so only a side is established.
